To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
trade liberalization and trade adjustment policies are complementary in the presence of adjustment needs and limited enforcement of international trade commitments.

trade adjustment assistance may be necessary to achieve reciprocal trade liberalization in the absence of perfect enforcement of trade agreements, and that the optimal trade adjustment policy will treat resources differently depending on whether they are employed in traded or non-traded sectors.

(i) if trade agreements are self-enforcing, the presence of adjustment subsidies can facilitate reciprocal trade agreements, (ii) if adjustment subsidies are used in this context they are likely to be used to subsidize resources that are not traded, (iii) if trade agreements can be enforced, then the presence of adjustment policies is not necessary to achieve trade agreements, and (iv) if trade agreements cannot be enforced, adjustment subsidies can be used to facilitate trade agreements even when they do not target resources
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between trade liberalization and adjustment policies.
the relationship between trade policy and trade adjustment policy.
the following questions: 1) How do adjustment policies interact with international trade policy?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are circumstances in which trade adjustment assistance can be welfare improving and that these circumstances are likely to be important in the context of trade liberalization.

trade adjustment subsidies can help to sustain reciprocal trade liberalization in economies that are characterized by adjustment costs and that are attempting, but not necessarily able, to sustain cooperative but non-self-enforcing international trade agreements.
the relationship between trade liberalization and adjustment assistance is ambiguous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the efficiency of trade liberalization depends crucially on how well trade agreements can be enforced, and that trade adjustment policies can be used to facilitate the enforcement of international trade rules.
the trade adjustment subsidy is an efficient policy for a country to use to sustain trade liberalization.
trade adjustment assistance can be a useful tool for promoting reciprocal trade agreements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between trade liberalization and trade adjustment subsidies is subtle, complex, and not necessarily obvious.
the design of trade adjustment assistance programs may have implications for international trade policy.
trade adjustment policies are not necessarily inefficient, even in the context of a model with a single factor of production.
